title_en: MSCI removes BRPT and BRMS from its global index, 7 Indonesian stocks dropped from Small Cap; US dollar strengthens, yen nears 160, gold below US$4,000
summary_en: MSCI's November 2026 review, released Thursday morning WITA, removes Barito Pacific (BRPT) and Bumi Resources Minerals (BRMS) from the MSCI Indonesia Index, with no Indonesian stocks added. In global markets, the US dollar strengthened sharply after hot US inflation data, pressuring the euro, yen and gold.
key_points_en: MSCI's official Global Standard Indexes list (11 Nov) shows two deletions from the MSCI Indonesia Index: Barito Pacific (BRPT) and Bumi Resources Minerals (BRMS). No Indonesian stocks were added.
According to CNBC Indonesia and Katadata, BRMS moves to the MSCI Indonesia Small Cap Index, while seven stocks are removed from Small Cap: AVIA, CTRA, MTEL, EMTK, JSMR, RAJA and WIFI.
Changes take effect after the close of trading on 30 November 2026 and are effective 1 December. MSCI's next review is scheduled to be announced on 9 February 2027 (CNBC Indonesia).

Reuters (11 Nov): the US dollar index rose 0.68% to 102.90, close to its high for the year. The euro fell 0.65% to about US$1.11, its lowest since May 2025, and the dollar rose to 159.84 yen. The probability of a 25 bp Fed rate hike in December rose to 87% (CME FedWatch).
Spot gold fell to about US$3,987 per ounce, below US$4,000 (Kitco). According to Reuters, Bitcoin was then up 0.93% at US$74,460.
why_en: Removal of stocks from MSCI indexes usually triggers selling by foreign passive funds, which can affect capital flows and the rupiah. A dollar strengthening on expectations of Fed rate hikes also tends to pressure emerging market currencies and risk assets, including crypto.
body_en: MSCI announced its November 2026 index review results on Wednesday (11/11) local time, or Thursday morning (12/11) Indonesian time. In MSCI's official Global Standard Indexes list, the MSCI Indonesia Index shows zero additions and two deletions: PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) and PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS). The list uses price data up to 20 October 2026, and MSCI says results may still be updated for corporate events or other adjustments before the effective date.

According to CNBC Indonesia and Katadata, BRMS does not leave the MSCI index family entirely, as it enters the MSCI Indonesia Small Cap Index, while BRPT is not listed as joining Small Cap. In the Small Cap category, seven stocks were removed: PT Avia Avian Tbk (AVIA), PT Ciputra Development Tbk (CTRA), PT Dayamitra Telekomunikasi Tbk (MTEL), PT Elang Mahkota Teknologi Tbk (EMTK), PT Jasa Marga (Persero) Tbk (JSMR), PT Rukun Raharja Tbk (RAJA) and PT Solusi Sinergi Digital Tbk (WIFI). There are no changes in the MSCI Micro Cap Indexes for Indonesian stocks.

All changes will be made after the close of trading on 30 November 2026 and take effect on 1 December 2026. CNBC Indonesia noted MSCI's next review is scheduled to be announced on 9 February 2027, effective 1 March 2027.

In global markets, the US dollar strengthened sharply. According to Reuters, the dollar index rose 0.68% to 102.90 on Wednesday. According to FXStreet, the year-to-date high is 102.94, reached in October. The euro fell 0.65% to about US$1.11, its lowest since May 2025, while the dollar rose 0.69% to 159.84 yen, its strongest in over two months and close to the psychological 160 level. The trigger was higher-than-expected US October inflation and hawkish comments from Fed officials. According to CME FedWatch as cited by Reuters, the probability of a 25 bp rate hike in December rose to 87% from about 70% a month ago.

Gold was also pressured. Kitco reported spot gold fell more than 1% to about US$3,987 per ounce, breaking below the US$4,000 level. A stronger dollar makes gold more expensive for buyers outside the US, and high interest rates reduce the appeal of non-yielding assets. On the crypto side, Reuters noted Bitcoin rose 0.93% to US$74,460 and Ether rose 1.19% to US$2,079 at the time of its report.
analysis_en: The market had long anticipated the removal of BRPT and BRMS, so what to watch is selling pressure ahead of 30 November and the direction of foreign funds afterwards. A strong dollar usually pressures the rupiah, and for users of local crypto exchanges, the rupiah exchange rate also determines crypto prices in rupiah. This is interpretation, not investment advice.
